report_name: DCSA Report: Foreign Spies Target US Defense Industry

threat_actors.name: Foreign Intelligence Entities (FIEs)
threat_actors.description: Foreign intelligence entities, primarily from the East Asia and Pacific region, targeting the U.S. defense industrial base through social engineering and exploitation of experts to acquire sensitive technology and information.
threat_actors.goals: Acquire sensitive U.S. technology and information from the defense industrial base.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing for Information
attack_patterns.description: Foreign intelligence entities used various lures, such as paid consultations, fake job offers, and conference invitations, to elicit information from subject matter experts in the U.S. defense industry.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Email was the primary vector (30% of attempts) used by foreign intelligence entities for initial contact with targets in the U.S. defense industrial base.

attack_patterns.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
attack_patterns.description: Foreign intelligence entities actively seek out and build relationships with cleared experts, researchers, and engineers to gain their specialized knowledge. This was the most common tactic, accounting for 28% of incidents.

attack_patterns.name: Search Open Websites/Domains
attack_patterns.description: Foreign intelligence entities use publicly available information from platforms like LinkedIn to identify and target cleared personnel in the U.S. defense industry.

identities.name: U.S. Cleared Defense Industrial Base
identities.description: The primary target of foreign intelligence entities, comprising U.S. cleared personnel and contractors working with sensitive or classified defense technology.

identities.name: U.S. Cleared Defense Personnel
identities.description: Subject matter experts, researchers, and engineers within the U.S. defense industrial base targeted by foreign intelligence entities for their specialized knowledge.

infrastructure.name: FIE Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Infrastructure used for sending unsolicited emails with lures such as paid consultations and fake job offers to target U.S. defense experts.

indicators.name: Suspicious Unsolicited Professional Outreach Email
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Unsolicited Professional Outreach Email
id: 2a9b4c1d-8e7f-4a3b-9c1d-5e6f7a8b9c0d
status: experimental
description: 'Detects unsolicited emails containing keywords commonly used as lures by Foreign Intelligence Entities (FIEs) to target defense industry experts, as described in the DCSA FY2025 report.'
references:
  - https://www.dcsa.mil/About-Us/News/Article/Article/4603722/dcsa-report-details-foreign-efforts-to-exploit-experts-and-business-ties-to-acc/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1598
  - attack.t1566
level: medium
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'paid consultation'
    - 'expert network request'
    - 'talent acquisition'
    - 'conference invitation'
    - 'call for papers'
    - 'supplier relationship'
    - 'business partnership proposal'
  condition: keywords
indicators.description: Detects emails containing keywords related to common social engineering lures used by FIEs to target defense experts.
